title: Triangles: Similarity and the Basic Proportionality Theorem
seo_title: Triangles Class 10 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 6)
standard_text: Definitions, examples, counter examples of similar triangles; the Basic Proportionality Theorem and its converse; criteria for similarity of triangles (AA, SSS, SAS) (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 10 Triangles worksheet (NCERT Chapter 6): Basic Proportionality Theorem, similarity criteria, parallel lines in triangles, scale factors and shadow problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How it works

Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales theorem): a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio. If DE ∥ BC, then AD/DB = AE/EC. The converse is also true.

Criteria: AA (two pairs of equal angles), SSS (all sides in the same ratio), SAS (two sides in the same ratio and the included angles equal).

Example

In △ABC, DE ∥ BC, AD = 3 cm, DB = 6 cm, AE = 4 cm. Find EC.

AD/DB = AE/EC

3/6 = 4/EC

Answer: EC = 8 cm

Example

A 6 m pole casts a 4 m shadow. A tower casts a 28 m shadow at the same time. How tall is the tower?

6/4 = h/28

Answer: 42 m

Common mistakes

  • Mixing a part and a whole: AD/AB = AE/EC is wrong. Use AD/DB = AE/EC or AD/AB = AE/AC.
  • Adding the difference instead of multiplying by the scale factor.
  • Matching sides in the wrong order. Use the order of the letters in △ABC ~ △PQR.

faq.q: What is the Basic Proportionality Theorem?
faq.a: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to meet the other two sides at distinct points, it divides those two sides in the same ratio. It is also called Thales theorem.

faq.q: What are the criteria for similarity of triangles?
faq.a: AA (or AAA): two pairs of equal angles. SSS: the three pairs of sides are in the same ratio. SAS: two pairs of sides in the same ratio with the included angles equal.

faq.q: What is the difference between similar and congruent triangles?
faq.a: Congruent triangles have the same shape and size. Similar triangles have the same shape but may differ in size.

faq.q: How are shadows used with similar triangles?
faq.a: At the same time of day, an object and its shadow form triangles similar to those of another object, so height ÷ shadow length is the same for both.

items.q: △ABC has angles of 80° and 33°. △DEF has angles of 33° and 67°. Are the triangles similar?
items.e: The third angle of △ABC is 67°, so both triangles have angles 80°, 33° and 67°. Two pairs of equal angles: Yes, by AA similarity.

items.e: Only one pair of angles matches (59°). The other angles of △DEF are 67° and 54°, not 63° and 58°. No.

items.q: A girl 1.2 m tall walks away from the base of a lamp post at 1.5 m/s. The lamp is 3.6 m above the ground. Find the length of her shadow after 2 seconds.
items.e: Distance walked = 3 m. Similar triangles: shadow/(3 + shadow) = 1.2/3.6, so shadow = 1.5 m.

items.q: Vivaan is 1.5 m tall and casts a shadow 2 m long. At the same time, a tree casts a shadow 10 m long. How tall is the tree?
items.e: The sun's rays make similar triangles, so height ÷ shadow is the same: 1.5 ÷ 2 = h ÷ 10, h = 7.5 m.

items.q: △ABC ≡ △PQR. ∠A = 76° and ∠B = 38°. Find ∠R.
items.e: The letters match in order: ∠R matches ∠C. ∠C = 180° − 76° − 38° = 66°, so ∠R = 66°.

items.q: Meera is 1.7 m tall and casts a shadow 2.4 m long. At the same time, a tree casts a shadow 18 m long. How tall is the tree?

items.q: Kavya is 1.8 m tall and casts a shadow 2.4 m long. At the same time, a tree casts a shadow 20 m long. How tall is the tree?

items.q: △ABC ≡ △PQR with AB = 14 cm, BC = 4 cm and AC = 13 cm. What is the length of PQ?
items.e: In △ABC ≡ △PQR the order of the letters matches, so PQ corresponds to AB: 14 cm.

items.q: A vertical pole 6 m long casts a shadow 8 m long. At the same time a tower casts a shadow 28 m long. Find the height of the tower.
items.e: Pole/shadow = tower/shadow: 6/8 = h/28, so h = 21 m.

items.q: A vertical pole 10 m long casts a shadow 4 m long. At the same time a tower casts a shadow 28 m long. Find the height of the tower.

items.q: In △ABC, DE is parallel to BC, with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 5 cm, DB = 2 cm and DE = 5 cm. Find BC.
items.e: △ADE and △ABC are similar (equal corresponding angles). AB = 5 + 2 = 7. BC ÷ DE = AB ÷ AD, so BC = 5 × 7 ÷ 5 = 7 cm.

items.q: Nikhil is 1.5 m tall and casts a shadow 3 m long. At the same time, a tree casts a shadow 18 m long. How tall is the tree?

items.q: In △ABC, DE is parallel to BC, with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 5 cm, DB = 8 cm and DE = 6 cm. Find BC.
items.e: △ADE and △ABC are similar (equal corresponding angles). AB = 5 + 8 = 13. BC ÷ DE = AB ÷ AD, so BC = 6 × 13 ÷ 5 = 15.6 cm.
